training.instructions: Rate the present effect on lift service using verified closures and usable routes.
criteria: Routine work or unconfirmed reports with no verified loss of service.
A limited outage with an alternative in service.
All lift service unavailable with no alternative and urgent access needs.
rows: Print the help number on the button label. Checks found the lifts operating normally.
Add 'emergency lift loss' to the response cards. This is a wording change and the lift log shows every car in service.
The dispatcher wanted a copy of the prior closure notice. It does not apply today and riders can use every lift.
Car B stopped accepting calls. Riders on its floors are using car A.
Power failed at one shaft. The accessible lift by the entrance is moving riders to every floor.
Every lift stopped and the stair bypass is closed. No one can reach the elevated ward where urgent access is required.

training.instructions: Grade the effect on the distribution happening now. Assess scope, service and available substitutes.
criteria: Low: ordinary requests with delivery continuing.
Medium: a local stoppage with delivery maintained through an alternative.
High: delivery stopped everywhere and no substitute can meet the urgent need.
rows: Revise the recipient field on the delivery slip. All ration points are serving their queues.
People are sharing an old post saying nobody can get supplies. The opening register and new receipts show every point is serving today.
The survey asks what emergency step staff would take if every route closed. No route closed, and all scheduled deliveries went out.
The hill ration desk closed because its key broke. Its visitors are receiving their allotments at a mobile desk outside.
One route was flooded. Teams are making its deliveries using the parallel road.
Every route was flooded and no desks have any stock. The emergency shelters need deliveries now and no alternate route is open.

training.instructions: Assign a level for the operational effect of the current report.
criteria: Routine request, advisory, or record change with no current interruption.
Part of the service has a confirmed interruption with a practical workaround.
No facility can supply clean linen and there is no workaround for urgent demand.
rows: The address printed on the linen bags needs to change. All wards received their usual clean linen.
The planning note describes simultaneous washer failures. There has been no failure and today's loads ran normally.
The manager wants a list of equipment by age. No department reported a delivery issue.
One washer is out of service. Staff are moving its loads to the smaller machine and delivering clean linen on that route.
One building's linen intake is inaccessible. A staffed intake next door is accepting its loads.
All wash equipment and emergency stock were contaminated. No department can get clean linen from any facility for the urgent intake.

training.instructions: Rate the present effect on entry to the arena. Use verified closures and substitutes.
criteria: Normal access, routine updates or tests without a closure.
Some entry routes closed while a usable substitute remains.
All entry routes are closed and urgent entry has no substitute.
rows: The ticket printer needs the new map with the closure symbols. All gates are open.
A contact asks for the article about last season's full closure. Today's entrance log has checks for every open gate.
Please add the staff sign-in link to the website. No access fault is stated.
The west ramp was closed after a rail snapped. The east ramp is taking the same visitors.
The main gate for one stand is jammed. Staff have opened its side gate and visitors are getting through.
The security relay locked every gate including the alternate ones. No one can enter for the urgent response inside.

training.instructions: Score actual processing disruption at present using the log and any working substitute.
criteria: No active processing disruption or urgent deadline.
A localized interruption with a workable processing route.
All processing stopped without a workaround and an immediate deadline.
rows: Rename the contact field in the next export. The log shows normal jobs completing in every queue.
The outage simulation raised a 'no route' banner. The real jobs have not been affected and all their receipts arrived.
We were asked when support ends for an older tool. The note doesn't describe a failure or a blocked job.
One group's queue stopped after an invalid update. It is using the live spare queue to complete the affected jobs.
The northern submitter cannot connect directly. It can still send the jobs through the working regional relay.
Job submission and both spare routes are down everywhere. The emergency processing deadline is now and no jobs can run.

training.instructions: Score current assembly evidence for the named display. Count the installed frame and verified panel as separate completed steps.
criteria: Neither required step has been completed for this display.
Exactly one required step has been completed for this display.
Both required steps have been completed for this display.
rows: The crew and panel checker have been assigned. The current display has no installed frame or verification record yet.
The two signatures belong to the trial display that was taken down. The display in the main room has no signed step.
The warehouse stored the frames next to the panels. This inventory list records no installation or panel check.
The frame is bolted into the current display. The checker has booked the panel review but has not done it.
The checker verified the panel for this display. The frame delivery is still pending.
The current display's frame is installed and its panel passed verification. Both records identify the display in the west room.
The record for the main display has the installation receipt and the checked panel signature. The old practice display failed inspection and was taken down.

training.instructions: Grade the completed evidence for the current cold room. Two separate checks are required: an actual temperature reading and an actual door seal inspection.
criteria: No completed check for this cold room.
Exactly one completed check for this cold room.
A completed temperature reading and door seal check for this cold room.
rows: A thermometer and a seal gauge are in the toolkit. Neither reading nor seal inspection was performed for this room.
The audit form lists a reading and inspection as planned. Both completion cells are blank.
The records show a signed reading and seal result for room C. This audit covers room B, which has no record.
The technician logged the temperature for this room. The seal inspection is booked for next week.
The current room's seal was inspected and signed. The temperature document attached is from another room.
The technician recorded this room's temperature and completed its seal inspection. Both signed entries name the same room and date.
The completed seal check and current temperature reading are recorded for room Q. The adjacent room's missing reading is outside this audit.

training.instructions: Score verified attendance at this race briefing. One registration is required for the captain and one for the safety guide.
criteria: No actual checked-in attendee in either required role.
Exactly one of the two required roles has a verified check-in.
Both required roles have a verified check-in at this briefing.
rows: The captain and safety guide are on the invitation list. The gate log has no actual check-ins and the briefing has not opened.
Someone checked in both roles for yesterday's practice. There is no arrival or online join record for today's briefing.
The captain and guide said they were planning to attend. Neither signed the roll or appeared at the video check-in.
The captain signed the race briefing roll. The guide received the calendar invite but did not attend.
The guide signed in at the actual briefing. The captain's check-in was recorded only for a different race.
The organizer verified both the captain and safety guide at today's briefing and checked them in under their roles.
Both required roles are recorded as present in this race briefing. The catering lead did not attend and is irrelevant to the rule.

training.instructions: Count completed safety checks for the exact repair bench: measured voltage and tested emergency stop.
criteria: Neither completed check for this bench.
Exactly one of the two checks completed for this bench.
Both the voltage measurement and stop test completed for this bench.
rows: The duty list assigns somebody to measure voltage and test the stop. No result has been entered for either check.
The meter and stop-test card were moved to the bench. The shift ended before anyone performed a check.
Bench L has two completed tests. This request is for bench G, whose status page contains no check results.
A signed voltage reading names this bench. The emergency stop test is waiting for a witness.
The stop test passed on this bench today. The only completed voltage measurement names the bench next to it.
The technician measured voltage and tested the emergency stop on the bench in this ticket. Both outcomes are documented against its serial number.
The current bench has its signed voltage reading and a successful stop test. The withdrawn test record refers to a different unit.

training.instructions: Score verified approval of this script revision. Count editorial signoff and technical signoff independently for this revision.
criteria: No completed approval for this script revision.
One completed approval for this script revision.
Both completed approvals for this script revision.
rows: Both review slots are booked and their names are on the agenda. The exact revision has no approvals yet.
The attached passes cover the rehearsal text. The final revision is separately stored and has no approval record.
The old approvals for the current text were withdrawn and neither reviewer has signed again.
Editorial approved revision D. Technical review is scheduled and has yet to start.
The technical reviewer approved revision E. Editorial signed an older revision and has not signed E.
Both reviewers signed for revision F and their records quote its exact checksum.
Revision G has completed technical and editorial review. The earlier revision was rejected, but the current one received both signatures.
